title: Product PRD + Roadmap + Pricing: Unified Inference v22
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview:

This document describes the Product Requirements (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference v22 (codename: "V22 / Predictable Edge"), Redwood Inference’s next major product increment focused on lower tail latency guarantees, predictable per-token economics for bursty workloads, and simplified enterprise packaging for Private deployments.

Audience:
- Product managers, engineering leads, platform and serving runtime engineers, sales and revenue, customer success, and SRE.

Goals (top-level):
1) Reduce 95th/99th percentile text-generation latency by 20–30% for common conversational workloads.
2) Reduce cost-per-token for bursty traffic patterns by 15% through improved burst routing + dynamic batching.
3) Deliver a clear, enterprise-friendly pricing tier for Private deployments with optional managed support and KMS/HSM add-ons.
4) Provide a low-friction migration path from v21 with compatibility and rollout automation.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Production P95 latency (text gen, 512-token average): target <= 240ms within three months of GA.
- Tail latency (P99): reduce by >=20% vs baseline v21 within three months.
- Cost per 1M tokens for bursty workloads: -15% vs v21 under identical traffic profile.
- GA customer traction: 5 paying Dedicated/Private customers migrated in Q3 2027.
- Quality regressions: <1% of eval prompts show decreased output quality vs pinned baseline model.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: API compatibility, routing policies (latency/cost aware), batching improvements, KV/prefix cache improvements, quantization profile updates, orchestration changes for Private package, pricing tiers and documentation.
- Out of scope: model architecture changes, major UI redesign of the Console, and experimental research kernels beyond selected kernel optimizations.

PRD: Requirements (high level):
Functional requirements:
- FR1: Support a new route-level config: "burst_profile" with fields: burst_window_ms, burst_capacity_tokens, fallback_policy. This config must be available in REST and SDKs.
- FR2: Latency-aware routing policy: route decisions select target model variant (gpu-fast, gpu-cost, cpu-quantized) based on per-request SLO and recent node P90 latencies.
- FR3: Dynamic batching improvements: continuous batching engine must prioritize low-latency small requests while achieving improved throughput for bursts. Configurable knobs: target_batch_ms, max_tokens_per_batch, prefer_latency (boolean).
- FR4: KV cache persistence across short-lived worker restarts for non-sensitive prompts (TTL configurable).
- FR5: Quantization profiles: promote two new recommended profiles (q4_0_fast and q3_tf32) with backward-compatible model artifacts.
- FR6: Private packaging: updated Helm charts, Terraform module parameters for network/policy, documented upgrade and rollback steps, and a migration CLI to assist enterprise customers.
- FR7: Backwards-compatible API: maintain current REST endpoints; any additions must be non-breaking.

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR1: System must maintain existing availability SLOs: 99.9% monthly availability for hosted endpoints.
- NFR2: New routing decisions must respond in <=5ms added overhead on the request path (p95).
- NFR3: Documentation coverage: upgrade guides, breakage matrix, and SDK examples released at GA.
- NFR4: Feature flags for controlled rollout (canary, percentage rollout, immediate rollback).

Design specs (high level):
1) API and config:
- New Route config snippet (example):
  {
    "route": "chat.predict",
    "burst_profile": {
      "burst_window_ms": "2000",
      "burst_capacity_tokens": "2000",
      "fallback_policy": "multi-variant"
    },
    "routing_policy": "latency_cost_aware",
    "quant_profile": "q4_0_fast"
  }
- Provide SDK helpers to construct burst_profile and routing_policy shorthand.

2) Runtime changes (serving runtime):
- Continuous batching: update scheduler to a hybrid token-and-time-based algorithm. The scheduler will maintain a short-latency lane for requests flagged prefer_latency and a throughput lane for batched bursts.
- Smart routing: augment the routing table with live node metrics (P50/P90/P99 latencies, GPU memory headroom, recent error rate). Use exponential decay window (30s) for metrics.
- KV caching: add optional WAL-backed KV persistence (configurable per-route). Eviction policy LRU with weighted prefix scoring.
- Kernel selection: include heuristics to pick q3_tf32 vs q4_0_fast based on sequence length distribution and memory constraints.

3) Orchestration and Private deploy packaging:
- Helm chart v2.0 with separate charts for control-plane and data-plane, clearer CRD for capacity pools, and optional HSM integration hooks.
- Terraform module inputs: enable_private_mode (bool), kms_provider (string), default_route_policy (string), reserved_gpu_ids (list of strings). Provide example usage in docs.

4) Observability and SLOs:
- New dashboards: route-level burst metrics, queue-time heatmaps, routing-decision breakdown (percent routed to each variant), and cost-per-token time series.
- Alerts: P95 latency above target for 5m, burst queue > 95th percentile for 10m, and routing-fallback rate > 2% for sustained 5m.

Roadmap and themes (quarterly):
- Q2 2027 (GA target window): complete implementation, wide internal dogfooding, initial Dedicated/Private pilot customers.
- Q3 2027: enterprise migrations, pricing tier launch, and optimization based on telemetry (reduce P99 tail).
- Q4 2027: expanded region support, additional quant profiles, and deeper Console integrations (per-route auto-tuning suggestions).

Prioritization and milestones:
- M1 (2027-05-10 GA): API additions, continuous batching hybrid scheduler, smart routing prototype, quant profiles, basic Private packaging, documentation.
- M2 (2027-06-15): Observability dashboards, rollout automation (percent canary), SDK updates.
- M3 (2027-08-01): Billing + pricing tier enablement, Dedicated capacity mapping, migration CLI.

Pricing and packaging notes:
- Pricing goals: be transparent, predictable for customers with bursty traffic, and align enterprise Private pricing with managed support tiers.
- New tiers (recommended):
  - Starter (hosted, pay-as-you-go): unchanged base per-token price; free 30-day trial credits.
  - Scale (hosted + Dedicated burst pools): discounted per-token rate for reserved throughput commitments (monthly commit), include auto-burst credits.
  - Enterprise Private (on-prem/VPC): platform license + per-node throughput licensing; optional Managed Add-on includes 24x7 on-call, quarterly optimizations, and upgrade assistance.

Pricing mechanics (high level):
- Introduce "burst credits" accounting: committed customers receive monthly burst credits convertible to tokens. Unused credits roll over up to 3 months. Bursts beyond credits billed at on-demand premium.
- Dedicated customers receive a throughput SLA and a discount curve for reserved capacity.
- Private customers sign a platform license (one-time or annual) + per-node throughput fee + optional managed support.

Packaging and Sales enablement:
- Sales collateral: one-pager comparing Scale vs Enterprise Private, migration checklist, TCO calculators demonstrating cost savings for bursty workloads.
- Legal: update contract templates to include burst credits clause, dedicated capacity commitments, and data-residency addendum for Private.

Migration and release plan (rollout):
1) Internal canary (Week 0): run V22 behind feature flags for 10% internal traffic; monitor degradation and routing behavior.
2) External controlled beta (Week 2): invite 3 pilot customers for Private/Dedicated migrations. Use migration CLI and provide concierge support.
3) Gradual public rollout (Weeks 4–8): staged percentage rollout with automated rollback on alert triggers.
4) GA (Week 8): full rollout plus pricing tier activation for new customers.

Runbook highlights for incidents during rollout:
- Owner: oncall-routing (eng-serving-runtime) and oncall-platform (eng-platform).
- Immediate mitigation steps: 1) flip routing feature flag to previous policy; 2) reduce batch target_batch_ms to 0 to disable batching; 3) reassign traffic to legacy model variant.
- Postmortem expectations: two-week turnaround for internal postmortem, with action items tracked in eng-platform retrospectives.

Release notes (v22) - 2027-05-10:
- Summary: Unified Inference v22 introduces latency-aware routing, hybrid continuous batching, burst_profile route configs, two new quantization profiles (q4_0_fast, q3_tf32), and updated Private packaging for easier enterprise migration.
- Notable API additions: route.burst_profile, routing_policy=latency_cost_aware, new SDK helpers (python, go, js). No breaking changes to existing endpoints.
- Performance: internal benchmarks show -25% median latency for short conversational requests and -18% P99 reduction in canary environments.
- Observability: new Grafana dashboards and Prometheus metrics: redwood.burst.queue_time_ms, redwood.routing.fallback_rate, redwood.cost.per_token.
- Migration notes: use provided migration CLI to convert existing route configs. Customers on Dedicated with reserved capacity must update capacity_pool labels to include burst_pool=true to enable burst routing.
- Known issues:
  - K1: WAL-backed KV persistence increases worker memory by ~5% in edge cases. Workaround: disable persistence per-route if memory constrained.
  - K2: A small percent (<=1%) of long sequence workloads may favor q3_tf32 which can change tokenization boundaries; ensure evals before pinning profiles.

Appendices:
A) Example CLI migration steps:
1. Install migration tool: curl -fsSL https://pkg.redwood.ai/migrate/v22.sh | bash
2. Dry-run: redwood-migrate --route chat.predict --dry-run > migrate-dryrun.json
3. Apply: redwood-migrate --route chat.predict --apply --backup=/tmp/migrate-backup.json

B) Sample route config (YAML):
---
route: chat.predict
routing_policy: latency_cost_aware
burst_profile:
  burst_window_ms: 2000
  burst_capacity_tokens: 2000
  fallback_policy: multi-variant
quant_profile: q4_0_fast
